--- Concepts ---

Non-dilutive funding
Grants that do not require giving up equity or repaying the capital are known as non-dilutive funding. This is highly sought after by early-stage startups to preserve founder ownership.

STEM
Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics. In Germany, this is commonly referred to as MINT (Mathematik, Informatik, Naturwissenschaft, Technik). Many public startup grants and academic funding programs specifically target these disciplines.

The Ask
In startup pitching, the ask is the specific request made to the audience, such as a funding amount, strategic introductions, or hiring needs.

Pitch Deck
A brief presentation used to provide an audience, usually investors, with a quick overview of your business plan, product, and growth traction.

ZETA
The speaker likely means ZETA (Center for Entrepreneurship at TU Clausthal), which focuses on automation, digitalization, and startup support.

EXIST-Gründerstipendium
A major German federal grant program for university startups, providing living expenses, materials, and coaching for up to one year.

--- Answers ---

Niedersachsen startup grant criteria
The Gründungsstipendium Niedersachsen funds innovative, digital, or sustainable startups with up to 2,000 EUR per month per founder for 8 months. Eligible projects must focus on technological innovation, social entrepreneurship, or ecological sustainability, rather than purely traditional commercial business models.

Pitch deck vs business plan
A pitch deck is a brief, highly visual 10-20 slide presentation used to spark investor interest. A business plan is a detailed, text-heavy document outlining operational and financial strategies.

German startup legal forms
Common options are a GmbH (minimum 25,000 EUR share capital, limited liability) or a UG (often called a mini-GmbH, starting with 1 EUR share capital).

--- Suggestions ---

EXIST-Gründungsstipendium
A major German government grant for university-affiliated startups. It provides monthly living stipends for up to one year, plus funding for materials and coaching, to help transition academic or STEM research into a viable business.

Hannover Messe
The speaker is referring to Hannover Messe, the world's leading trade fair for industrial technology. Held annually in Hanover, Germany, it focuses on automation, digitalization, energy systems, and industrial startups.

Clausthal-Zellerfeld
The speaker likely means Clausthal, a university town in Niedersachsen known for the TU Clausthal and its active startup support programs.

Guy Kawasaki's 10/20/30 Rule
A classic pitch deck framework: 10 slides, 20 minutes maximum presentation time, and using at least a 30-point font size to keep slides clear and readable.

The Curse of Knowledge
A cognitive bias where experts assume others have the background to understand their jargon. Avoid technical terms to keep your pitch accessible to general investors.

Tailoring the pitch deck
No, customize your pitch deck for each audience. Investors need financial returns, corporate partners focus on integration and security, and customers care about solving their immediate pain points.

Gründungsservice der TU Clausthal
The university's startup service offers free initial legal and tax consultations, coaching, and help applying for EXIST grants for local spin-offs.

Product-market fit
The speaker likely meant product-market fit: the degree to which a product satisfies a strong market demand, which is crucial for overcoming resistance in traditional industries.

Validating market acceptance
To test acceptability in traditional industries, run low-cost pilot projects or co-create solutions with a single trusted early adopter before a full launch.

Status quo bias
The preference for the current state of affairs, where any change from the baseline is perceived as a loss. This explains resistance to new systems in established industries.

First steps for founders
To get started, focus on customer discovery to validate the problem, map out a lean canvas, and identify the minimum viable product (MVP) needed to test core assumptions.

CfE
Center for Entrepreneurship — a common university department or hub dedicated to supporting student startups and business creation.

Gründungszentrum
German for startup incubator or business creation center, providing office space, resources, and advising for new companies.

Gemeinnützigkeit
German grants often require projects to demonstrate public interest or social impact (Gemeinnützigkeit) rather than pure commercial gain, aligning with the speaker's point about serving the community.

Non-repayable grants
While public grants like EXIST do not require equity or repayment, they are strictly earmarked. Founders must submit detailed usage reports, and misusing funds or failing to meet milestones can trigger repayment demands.

IdeenExpo Hannover
IdeenExpo is a major biennial youth education trade fair in Hannover, Germany. It focuses on science and technology (STEM) to get students excited about technical careers through hands-on exhibits.

Business Model Canvas
The core topics mentioned—problem, solution, customers, revenue, and team—are the foundational elements of the Business Model Canvas, a strategic tool used to quickly map out a new business idea.

Incubator vs Accelerator
In Germany, use incubators for early-stage validation and local network building, and accelerators later to scale and prepare for venture capital rounds.

Pitch deck presentation length
While the pitch itself is often 3 to 5 minutes, standard pitch decks contain 10 to 15 slides to allow for Q&A and deeper follow-up discussions.

Securing testing partners
To secure factory testing partners, offer a zero-cost pilot with a clear liability waiver and a defined, low-risk scope that does not disrupt their main production line.

Regulatory Sandbox
Consider using a regulatory sandbox (Reallabor) in Germany. It allows startups to test innovative technologies and business models under relaxed regulatory requirements.

Integration und Sprachförderung
Ausländische Gründer können in Deutschland durch Programme wie 'IQ Netzwerk' oder lokale Handelskammern (IHK) gezielte Unterstützung bei Behördengängen und Fachsprache erhalten.

Legal resources for German startups
Founders in Germany can access free initial legal consultations through local Chambers of Commerce (IHK) or specialized university startup networks.

Starting a business in Germany
Non-EU founders typically need a residence permit for self-employment (Section 21 AufenthG), requiring a viable business plan, local economic interest, and secured financing.

Academic Spin-off Mindset
Transitioning from research to business requires shifting focus from technical perfection to market validation, customer discovery, and commercial viability.

Hacker, Hustler, Hipster
A classic framework for balanced startup teams: the Hacker builds the tech, the Hustler drives the business and sales, and the Hipster designs the user experience.

Industrial IoT (IIoT)
The integration of automation, AI, and machine learning in factory workflows is commonly referred to as Industrial IoT or Industry 4.0.

Gründungshochschule
The speaker likely means 'Gründungshochschule' or 'Gründungs-Bootcamp' (entrepreneurship school/program) rather than a literal 'preschool' for children.

EXIST English Applications
The EXIST-Gründerstipendium (EXIST) has officially accepted applications and project proposals in English since 2018.

WiReGo
Wirtschaftsförderung Region Goslar — the regional economic development agency for the Goslar district, supporting local startups and businesses.
